lastText: File ClosedTanks Kept for Egypt, and Not EnoughContestedThe War Cabinet and Chiefs of Staff, 1939–1945End of hostilities: OCTOBER 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed with minor delayImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around October 1945: slower than the historical May 1945, the price of caution at the moments this campaign offered a faster, riskier road instead. The campaign reaches its end having spent more Western Allied lives than the historical record: the price of the bolder, more aggressive road at several of this campaign's genuine forks. Stalin was pressed hard on Poland's postwar government at Yalta rather than accepted on ambiguous terms: a harder line taken exactly where the historical conference chose accommodation. The stand in the Peloponnese broke and the beaches were lost, and what the Germans took in Greece was a division or more instead of the real 14,000. The Mediterranean Fleet was sent against the German convoys off Crete, as it was, and paid three cruisers and six destroyers for an island that was lost anyway. What was really being decided, choice by choice, was never whether Germany lost, only what the peace on the other side of it would look like.One Year LaterA year past victory in Europe, the machinery of occupation is running on the arrangements this campaign's own conferences (Tehran, Yalta, the ones this command actually attended) settled or failed to settle in advance.
